name: The Saudi Investment Bank (SAIB)
legal_name: The Saudi Investment Bank (a Saudi Joint Stock Company)
founded: 1976 (Royal Decree M/31, 23 Jun 1976, as The Saudi Investment Banking Corporation; operations began March 1977; IPO on Tadawul 1993; the SAIB name was adopted later and full commercial banking began after that)
ownership_summary: Tadawul-listed. The General Organization for Social Insurance (GOSI) is the major shareholder with 25.61% (2025 Board report); the FY2025 investor presentation shows 25.6% and foreign ownership of 10.7% (Jan 2025). Share capital SAR 12.5bn (bonus issues in 1Q 2022 and 1Q 2024). No other holder above 5% is named in the sources read.
government_link: Yes (indirect). GOSI, a Saudi government social-insurance institution, holds 25.61% (Board report 2025, S1). Percentage date taken as year-end 2025 (report year).
group_structure: Parent bank with 3 wholly owned subsidiaries: Alistithmar for Financial Securities and Brokerage Company (Alistithmar Capital, 'ICAP'; CMA licensed; capital SAR 250m; profiled separately as sa-alistithmar-capital), The Saudi Investment Real Estate Company (holds title deeds as collateral; capital SAR 500,000) and SAIB Markets Limited Company (Cayman; derivatives and repo for the bank). Associates and joint ventures: American Express (Saudi Arabia) 50% (card issuing), Yanal Finance Company 38% (lease financing) and Amlak International Finance Company 22.4% (Shariah-compliant real estate, SME and consumer finance). The bank also consolidates a few real estate funds (Q2 2026 FS note 7). Double counting: Alistithmar Capital's assets, income and AUM sit inside the bank's 'Asset Management and Brokerage' segment. Do not add sa-alistithmar-capital figures to this record.

subsidiaries.name: Alistithmar for Financial Securities and Brokerage Company (Alistithmar Capital / ICAP)
subsidiaries.activity: Brokerage, asset management (funds and private portfolios), custody, investment banking advisory (CMA licence 11156-37)

subsidiaries.name: The Saudi Investment Real Estate Company
subsidiaries.activity: Holds title deeds as collateral for the bank's real estate lending

subsidiaries.name: SAIB Markets Limited Company (Cayman Islands)
subsidiaries.activity: Derivatives and repurchase activities on behalf of the bank

subsidiaries.name: American Express (Saudi Arabia) (joint venture)
subsidiaries.activity: Credit cards and other American Express products in KSA

subsidiaries.name: Amlak International Finance Company (associate)
subsidiaries.activity: Shariah-compliant real estate, SME and consumer financing

footprint: Saudi Arabia only. 49 branches at 2Q 2026 (50 at end-2025), 328 ATMs and ITMs and over 10,000 POS terminals at end-2025; 3 dedicated conventional branches; 3 regional corporate offices (Riyadh, Jeddah, Al Khobar) (S1, S4). Head office Riyadh.
customer_segments: Four segments by 2Q 2026 share of operating income: Treasury and Investments 34%, Corporate 33%, Retail 25% (including the Silver, Gold and Platinum programmes and Private Banking), Asset Management and Brokerage 8% (S4). Also public institutions, SMEs. Personal banking is Shariah-focused, with a smaller conventional offer.
business_lines: Retail (Personal Banking: Silver mass, Gold and Platinum premium, Private Banking for HNW), Corporate Banking, Public Institutions, Treasury and Investment Group (ALM, FX, structured products, investment portfolio, financial-institution partnerships), and Asset Management and Brokerage through Alistithmar Capital. FY2025 income before zakat by segment (SAR '000): Asset Management and Brokerage 143,940 (2024: 116,371); corporate 1,682,097; treasury and investments 1,014,594 (S1 segment note). H1 2026: Asset Management and Brokerage operating income SAR 177m (+29%) and pre-zakat income SAR 113m (+47%), driven by fund management fees (+36% fee income) and margin income (S3). Joint venture in cards with American Express. Fintech VC arm S60 Ventures (USD 100m fund managed by Alistithmar Capital, 2025).

capabilities.wealth_summary: SAIB is a conventional bank with a Shariah-focused personal banking offer (deposits compliant with Shariah controls were SAR 58.3bn of SAR 109.6bn at end-2025). Retail has Silver (mass), Gold and Platinum (premium) programmes and a Private Banking programme for HNW clients run by dedicated relationship managers; no eligibility thresholds are published. Investment products come from its 100%-owned Alistithmar Capital, which manages SAR 40.5bn (31 Dec 2025; SAR 21.7bn Shariah-approved) and offers funds, brokerage and real estate; Private Banking clients get reduced or waived fund subscription fees and trading commissions. The Asset Management and Brokerage segment is about 8% of operating income (H1 2026), with fee income +36% on fund management fees. Strategy 2027 (43 initiatives, refreshed in Q4 2025) targets accelerating profitable growth in Private Banking and building a differentiated Affluent proposition with a new mobile app; the Q2 2026 outlook says SAIB will expand fee-based businesses including asset management and brokerage. A CEO change took effect on 1 Oct 2026 (Deputy CEO Salman Al-Fughom replaced Faisal Al-Omran).

segments.name: Silver
segments.eligibility: Entry-level programme; criteria 'based on salary, average balance or instant deposits' but no amounts published (S1, S9)

segments.name: Gold
segments.eligibility: Premium-tier programme; no amounts published. Page cites a 'wide range of investment and financing products'.

segments.name: Platinum
segments.eligibility: Premium-tier programme with a dedicated Relationship Manager; no amounts published

segments.name: Private Banking
segments.eligibility: Not published ('high-net-worth customers'). Dedicated Relationship Manager, Visa Infinite Privilege card, family-member programme (up to 5 first-degree relatives), reduced or waived fees on safe deposit boxes, investment fund subscriptions and trading commissions.

private_banking.detail: Private Banking is described as 'the pinnacle' of the offer, managed by dedicated expert Relationship Managers. Benefits: Visa Infinite Privilege card, airport lounges, concierge, family-member programme, loyalty programmes (Aseel, WooW), reduced or waived fees on investment fund subscriptions and trading commissions, and 'Special Investment Products through Alistithmar Capital' (brokerage, asset management, real estate investments). 2025: new segmentation and KYC onboarding for Affluent and Private Banking customers; commercial real estate financing launched for them. Strategy: accelerate profitable growth (revisit segments and RM coverage, revamp value proposition and key journeys). Retail lending including private banking grew 2% in H1 2026. Head of Private Banking not named in any source found.

asset_management.detail: Through Alistithmar Capital (100%): AUM SAR 40,526m at 31 Dec 2025, of which SAR 21,688m Shariah-approved (Board report). The bank's segment reports H1 2026 operating income SAR 177m (+29%) on fund management fees. See sa-alistithmar-capital.

brokerage.detail: Through Alistithmar Capital: Saudi and international brokerage with margin finance (see sa-alistithmar-capital). Bank site links it as 'Investment Services - Al-Istithmar Capital'.

digital_investing.detail: Bank apps (new retail SAIB Mobile app, rated 4.8 on Apple and Google; Travel App; Easy Pay; Flexx Safe) do not list investing, funds or brokerage features on the apps page. Trading and fund subscription run in Alistithmar Capital's separate trading app and web portal (login link on the bank site). The bank app offers a Daily Savings Account (Mudaraba, 3.5% compound profit, Zakat-exempt) opened only in the app.

advisory.detail: Dedicated relationship managers for Platinum and Private Banking (S8, S9). Alistithmar Capital holds a CMA advising licence (see sa-alistithmar-capital). Investment advice content for retail clients is not described on the bank's pages.

discretionary.detail: Alistithmar Capital manages mutual funds and private portfolios under investment policy guidelines (see sa-alistithmar-capital). The bank itself offers no discretionary service in the sources read.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advisor or model-portfolio product found on the bank or Alistithmar Capital sites. The 2025 Board report mentions an analytics-powered CRM for Corporate and Public Institutions RMs and data and AI use cases, not investing products.

funds_platform.detail: In-house Alistithmar Capital funds (nine public funds and a REIT) are subscribed through the Alistithmar Capital mutual fund portal and app; Private Banking clients get fee reductions. No third-party fund shelf found.

structured_products.detail: The Treasury and Investment Group manages 'foreign exchange trading, structured products, and the Bank's investment portfolio and derivative products' (Board report). Alistithmar Capital's Shariah governance text lists structured products among its Shariah-compliant offers. No product details, issuers or client eligibility published.

private_markets.detail: Through Alistithmar Capital: real estate funds (2025 launches are in sa-alistithmar-capital) and S60 Ventures, a USD 100m fintech venture fund managed by Alistithmar Capital (2025). The Private Banking page lists real estate investments via Alistithmar Capital.

islamic_wealth.detail: Shariah-compliant deposits (SAR 58.3bn), Murabaha, Tawarruq and Ijarah financing (SAR 74.4bn), Mudaraba savings account, and Shariah-compliant Alistithmar Capital funds. Conventional equivalents also exist.

initiatives.what: Rolled out the new retail mobile app to all customers (4.8 rating); launched an app-only Daily Savings Account (Mudaraba); Google Pay integration; Huawei AppGallery release; new segmentation and revamped KYC onboarding for Affluent and Private Banking customers; commercial real estate financing for them

S60 Ventures: USD 100m fintech venture fund managed by Alistithmar Capital; refreshed Strategy 2027 in Q4 2025 with additional priorities for 2026-2027 (product development, digital capabilities, data and analytics, customer experience, sales effectiveness)
H1 2026 release outlook: continued growth in corporate and private banking, further development of the retail offer, and expansion of fee-based businesses including asset management and brokerage
Board accepted CEO Faisal Al-Omran's resignation (effective 30 Sep 2026) and named Deputy CEO Salman Al-Fughom CEO effective 1 Oct 2026 after SAMA no-objection

opportunities: Strategy 2027 names Private Banking 'accelerate profitable growth' and Affluent 'build differentiated value proposition ... launch new mobile app' (S1 PDF p.10)
H1 2026 outlook: SAIB will 'expand fee-based businesses, including asset management and brokerage' for diversification; the segment grew fee income 36% (S3 pp.10-11)
Bank app lists no investing features; funds and trading sit in Alistithmar Capital's separate app and portal, so an in-app wealth journey is not evident (S10, S11)
No robo, model portfolio or third-party fund shelf found; Private Banking tier thresholds and wealth offer are not published (S8, S9)
New CEO from 1 Oct 2026 (previously Deputy CEO and long-time treasurer and CIO) and a refreshed strategy create a decision window (S13, S14)
barriers: Product shelf is in-house through Alistithmar Capital (CMA licence 11156-37); investment contracts would likely sit with the subsidiary (S1, S17)
Retail profitability is under pressure: H1 2026 retail pre-zakat income -69% YoY, fee income -42% (S3 p.8), which may constrain investment in new wealth technology
Mixed conventional and Shariah franchise: Shariah-compliant and conventional versions of products may both be needed (S1)
Executive transition (CEO changed 1 Oct 2026; Deputy CEO successor, Head of Private Banking and chief digital officer not named in sources found) (S13, S14)

discrepancies.detail: The Board report 2025 (5-year table) and the 4Q 2025 release give SAR 172,720m / SAR 172.7bn. The Q2 2026 FS comparative column labelled 'Audited' shows SAR 172,825,012 thousand. Customer deposits, net loans and equity agree across all three.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded the Q2 2026 FS comparative as the extra 31 Dec 2025 record with status 'Conflicting sources'. The difference is about 0.06%; a reclassification after the Board report is likely but not documented.

discrepancies.detail: Al-Fughom (bank bio), Al Fagham (Mubasher/Decypha), Al-Fughom (Enterprise AM, Alistithmar Capital page).
discrepancies.resolution: Used the bank's own spelling (Al-Fughom). Same person: former Deputy CEO.

discrepancies.detail: Mubasher/Decypha states 1 Oct 2026; Enterprise AM (30 Sep 2026) says 'tomorrow' without a date.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 1 Oct 2026; SAIB's Management Team page (checked 2026-10-13) lists the new CEO (S20).

discrepancies.detail: The Board report narrative lists income components that sum to about SAR 4.26bn, against reported total operating income of SAR 4,794m. The 4Q 2025 release attributes the difference to a one-off SAR 535m gain on sale of land.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded the reported total with a note on the one-off. FY2025 audited statements not opened.

discrepancies.detail: The Board report 2025 lists Feras Al-Sheikh as Acting Chief Risk Officer (from May 2025); SAIB's Management Team page (checked 2026-10-13) lists him as Chief Risk Officer.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the current official title (Chief Risk Officer); the date the acting status ended is not published.

discrepancies.detail: The Board report 2025 lists nine directors, including Mohammed Salem Mussa (non-executive); the official board page (checked 2026-10-13) lists eight and omits him. Decypha/Mubasher report that he died on 26 Sep 2026.
discrepancies.resolution: Not a profiled person in this file; recorded here and in open_items. It is unclear whether the official page omitted him all along or was updated after the reported death.

discrepancies.detail: Official board page: Head of Investment at Asila Investment Co.; Board report 2025: Chief Investment Officer, Assila Investments; earlier employer written NCB Capital (page) versus Alahli Capital Company (Board report).
discrepancies.resolution: Both wordings kept in the profile. Neither source says whether 'Alahli Capital' and 'NCB Capital' name the same former employer.

open_items: CEO change: Faisal Al-Omran left on 30 Sep 2026 and Salman Al-Fughom became CEO on 1 Oct 2026. SAIB's Management Team page (checked 2026-10-13) lists Al-Fughom as CEO and shows no Deputy CEO; the successor to the Deputy CEO role is not named in any source. SAIB's own announcement and the Tadawul filing were not opened (Saudi Exchange answers 403 to automated reads).

The official Management Team page (https://www.saib.com.sa/en/management-team, found 2026-10-13) names no head of Private Banking, Affluent or wealth and no chief digital officer; the Chief Personal Banking Officer (Khayat) and the COO (Alafaleq) remain the nearest owners. The same page lists, and this pass did not profile: Chief Compliance Officer (Badr Allaf), Chief Corporate Governance Officer (Monirah AlSwaydani), Chief Quality & Customer Care Officer and Acting Chief Transformation Officer (Thamer Al-Humayyd; he ran personal banking on an acting basis in 2023), Chief Internal Audit Officer and Chief Human Resources Officer. Consider adding Al-Humayyd if transformation counts as a digital/strategy decision-maker role.
Silver, Gold, Platinum and Private Banking eligibility thresholds are not published on the pages checked.
Q3 2026 (30 Sep 2026) results are not yet published at check date. Alistithmar Capital's funds already published Q3 2026 quarterly statements (see sa-alistithmar-capital).

FY2025 audited consolidated FS were not opened; FY2025 income uses the Board report and 4Q 2025 release. The 4Q 2025 total assets figure differs slightly from the Q2 2026 comparative (see discrepancies).
Customer figure (966k) does not say whether it is total or active, or retail only. Employee headcount not found.

LinkedIn: matches kept for the CEO, the Chief Personal Banking Officer (title not visible in the snippet) and the Alistithmar Capital CEO. LinkedIn role searches for the COO, Chief Treasury & Investment Officer and other executives, and news checks beyond those run on 2026-10-13, were not run because the WebSearch quota was exhausted during this pass (X27). Enterprise AM (30 Sep 2026, S14) links https://www.linkedin.com/in/faisal-al-omran-97a48415/ for the former CEO; not recorded (not an official link; profile not opened).
Saudi Exchange (saudiexchange.sa) announcement pages were not opened. The SAIB home-page navigation lists no wealth or priority-banking page beyond Private Banking and the customer programmes.

Board members not profiled: Yaser Al-Jarallah, Khalid Al-Rowais, Dr. Ghazi AlRawi, Hani AlSharif, Dr. Abdulaziz AlZoom (all on the official board page, 2026-10-13) and Mohammed Salem Mussa (Board report 2025; reported dead on 26 Sep 2026). The Board report 2025 committee table names a Shariah Committee (Dr. Abdulrahman Al Saadi, chair; Dr. Ibrahim AlLahim; Dr. Abdullah AlHamdan) that is also not profiled.

Alistithmar Capital's team page (checked 2026-10-13) is stale on SAIB roles: it still calls Al-Omran SAIB CEO and ICAP vice chairman and Al-Fughom SAIB Deputy CEO. Whether Al-Omran keeps his ICAP board seat is not documented (see sa-alistithmar-capital).
